summary: Adds an isSameOrigin(a, b) helper to ufo. The semantics are being agreed through a test spec first, which now compares ports strictly. The owner later asked for default-port equivalence instead.
narrative: The owner asked for an isSameOrigin(a, b) helper in ufo, with tests written first in test/same-origin.test.ts so the semantics could be agreed before implementing. The agent explored the existing helpers and wrote a spec based on WHATWG origin comparison (obs 3). The owner then asked for strict port handling, so https://example.com and https://example.com:443 do not match. The agent removed the default-port equivalence cases for http, https, ws and wss, switched to strict comparison and amended the file header to say ports are compared as written (obs 4-7). The implementation is deliberately left for later. In a separate conversation at 13:29 the owner reversed this and said default ports should count as the same origin, because their CDN rewrites links with an explicit :443. The spec will need rework before implementation.

milestones.text: Explored existing path-comparison helpers (isSamePath, isEqual) in src/utils.ts before adding isSameOrigin.
Created test/same-origin.test.ts with WHATWG-style origin semantics and no implementation.
Per the owner's request, removed default-port equivalence and switched the spec to strict port comparison.
Amended the spec header to state that ports are compared as written.
In another conversation, the owner reversed the port rule: default ports (:443, :80) should count as the same origin, to be handled at implementation.

preferences.preference: Agree on semantics through tests before any implementation.
preferences.quote: Before any implementation, write the test cases in a new test/same-origin.test.ts so we can agree on the semantics. Don't implement it yet.

preferences.preference: Prefers explicit behavior over implicit normalization, at least initially, and wants an explicit test case for each such rule.
preferences.quote: keep it strict. `https://example.com` and `https://example.com:443` should NOT count as the same origin, I don't want magic port normalization in there.

evidence: Prompts 1-2; observations 1-7; prompt 5 of the joinURL conversation
